report.summary: Louvain and Leiden are the most stable under incremental change, with Leiden offering better stability guarantees due to its guarantee of connectivity and refinement steps. Infomap is less stable because it optimizes for flow compression, which is sensitive to edge weight changes. Label propagation is fast but highly unstable, often reshuffling partitions with minor graph changes. risks: Leiden may still reshuffle if graph structure changes drastically (e.g., new repo added).
Stability metrics (NMI) can be misleading if partitions are trivially stable (e.g., all nodes in one community).
todos: Benchmark Leiden vs Louvain on a real multi-repo dependency graph with incremental commits.
Evaluate stability using NMI and Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) across consecutive snapshots.
Consider using 'ensemble clustering' to aggregate multiple runs for robustness.

handoff.suggestion: Implement Leiden with incremental update using the 'leidenalg' Python library. For each commit, run Leiden on the new graph but initialize with the previous partition to reduce reshuffling. Measure NMI between consecutive partitions; if NMI drops below a threshold (e.g., 0.9), flag the change. Also, consider using 'Consensus clustering' (Lancichinetti & Fortunato, 2012) to combine multiple runs for a stable representative partition.
